races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Restricted Novice Stakes (Horses In Bands B/C/D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Tickhill Flyer
runners_data.note: Unraced newcomer from strong yard with unknown style but excellent breeding suggests natural ability could show immediately
runners_data.comment: Half-brother to three winners; sole newcomer; interesting to see how he goes in betting
runners_data.spotlight: Ninth foal; Tasleet half-brother to winners Akeed Dubawi (1m AW; RPR 80), Tarnhelm (6f-1m; 72) and Billy McGarry (7f-8.6f; 66); dam 5f 2yo winner (90); sole newcomer but interesting to see how he goes in the betting.

runners_data.name: Agric Ranger
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and soundly beaten last time, needs significant improvement despite trainer having poor recent strike rate
runners_data.comment: Improvement possible but soundly beaten at 16-1 on his recent debut at Pontefract
runners_data.spotlight: 10,000gns foal whose unraced dam is from a speedy family; improvement is possible on this second start but he was soundly beaten at 16-1 at Pontefract (6f, good to soft) on his recent debut and needs a big step forward.

runners_data.name: The Untamed
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs strong pace to be effective, 21 days since solid debut second should have him spot on
runners_data.comment: Runner-up on debut on AW three weeks ago; could have plenty more to offer
runners_data.spotlight: Weak in the betting but still ran well when runner-up at 13-2 on debut at Chelmsford (6f, AW) three weeks ago; his dam was a useful 6f winner and he could have plenty more to offer; firmly in calculations.

runners_data.name: Vega Storm
runners_data.note: Another hold-up type who recovered from slow start on debut, likely wants further than 6f based on that running style
runners_data.comment: Eyecatching third on debut at Newcastle last month and could be sharper for that outing
runners_data.spotlight: 14-1, recovered from slow start to finish third of 11 on debut at Newcastle (6f, AW) four weeks ago; it's possible a longer trip will be preference but he could be sharper for that initial outing and is respected.

runners_data.name: Different Opinions
runners_data.note: Uncertain style but has shown ability over 7f, headgear applied suggests connections expect improvement from 11-day break
runners_data.comment: Has shown promise for top yard and the drop in trip could suit on his third start
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up on debut at Chelmsford (7f, AW) last March then failed to build on it when fourth at Southwell (7f, AW); however, he's in top hands and his pedigree suggests the drop in trip will suit; wears first-time blinkers and he remains one to be interested in.

runners_data.name: Mind Over Matter
runners_data.note: Natural front runner returning from 220-day break, previous good form at 6f on good ground makes him dangerous if ready
runners_data.comment: Good 2nd on debut last June; two lesser runs followed but leading claims if back to best
runners_data.spotlight: Good second on debut at Ayr (6f, good) last June; two lesser runs followed last year but he's from a useful sprinting family and is a leading contender if back to his best in a first-time hood, following a break.

runners_data.name: Milford Grange
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who showed promise last year but disappointed badly last time out despite suitable conditions
runners_data.comment: Promising third on sole 2yo start but disappointing at Pontefract nine days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Fared best of the newcomers when promising third at Redcar (6f, good) last October; far too soon to write him off but he was disappointing at Pontefract (6f, good to soft) nine days ago, even allowing for a wide trip.

runners_data.name: Kode Grey
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with fading finish tendency, needs everything to fall right and form figures suggest that's unlikely
runners_data.comment: Down the field at big odds this year on his first two starts (6f/7f, AW)
runners_data.spotlight: Down the field at big odds this year on his first two starts (6f/7f, AW) and considerable improvement is necessary.

races.paceDynamic: Mind Over Matter looks the sole committed front runner with his prominent style, setting up a sustainable tempo without early pressure from other pace angles. Milford Grange may track close but prefers to sit rather than lead, while the hold-up brigade of The Untamed, Vega Storm and Kode Grey will need the pace to develop. With limited early speed signed up, this becomes a tactical affair where Mind Over Matter can dictate terms from the front. This race shape clearly favours the early pace-setters and prominent racers who can avoid traffic problems in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner
scenarios.trigger: If Mind Over Matter gets an easy lead and controlled fractions
scenarios.body: Mind Over Matter can kick clear in the final furlong while the hold-up horses struggle to make up ground from the back. The lack of pace pressure allows him to save energy for a strong finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Milford Grange or Different Opinions can sit close and time their run perfectly
scenarios.body: The tracker gets first run on Mind Over Matter and benefits from a true pace without getting involved early. Previous good form at similar trips gives them the tactical edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes slow enough for closers to be effective
scenarios.body: The Untamed or Vega Storm get the perfect setup with a crawling pace that allows their finishing kicks to be devastating. The front runners pay for going too slow early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Newcomer Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Tickhill Flyer shows immediate ability on debut with natural speed
scenarios.body: The well-bred newcomer from the Parkinson/Smith yard breaks fast and either leads or presses throughout. His unknown style creates tactical chaos for the others.

watchPoints.text: Mind Over Matter's fitness after 220 days off could see him fold in the final furlong despite taking them along
Watch Tickhill Flyer's market moves and how he breaks from the stalls as unknown style could disrupt pace predictions
Different Opinions wearing headgear for first time suggests yard expects big improvement but could indicate temperament issues
The Untamed and Vega Storm need to see sustained gallop from 3f out to unleash their finishing kicks effectively
Milford Grange's recent Pontefract flop came on soft ground so return to good conditions could spark revival

races.name: Download The Raceday Ready App Restricted Novice Stakes (Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Sea And Sun
runners_data.comment: 33,000gns yearling by Sea The Moon; could give a good account on debut
runners_data.spotlight: 33,000gns yearling; third foal; dam 1m/8.6f AW winner (RPR 99), half-sister to useful winners Spangler (7f/1m including 2yo) and Kipps (1m2f 2yo); this Sea The Moon colt could give a good account on debut.

runners_data.name: Sun Lord
runners_data.comment: Useful pedigree and this Almanzor newcomer is one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth foal; Almanzor brother to French 1m2f 2yo winner The Sheriff, closely related to 1m2f-1m4f winner Wootton'sun (RPR 101); dam French 1m4f Flat/2m1f hurdle winner from classy family; this newcomer is one to consider.

runners_data.name: Picaro
runners_data.comment: First foal; dam French 11.7f winner; could have a part to play on debut; watch the betting
runners_data.spotlight: £10,000 yearling by Havana Gold; first foal; dam French 11.7f winner, half-sister to French 6.5f/7f winner Zalari, out of 1m Listed winner; Newmarket trainer is 2-10 with his Ripon runners; could have a part to play on debut, especially if strong in the betting.

runners_data.name: Rocky River
runners_data.comment: Tackles different trip on second start but always behind at 40-1 on debut in February (1m)
runners_data.spotlight: Pedigree indicates that the step up in trip will be in his favour but he was reluctant to load and always behind when 40-1 on debut at Newcastle (1m, AW) in February; may be best watched for now.

runners_data.name: Poppeye
runners_data.comment: 4yo who was fourth on AW on recent belated debut; could take step forward; not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: 4yo who made belated debut at Southwell (1m4f, AW) 11 days ago and was beaten 7l in fourth of nine; improvement is necessary but he's a half-brother to the yard's useful 1m2f-1m4f winner Real Terms and may well be able to take a step forward; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Urchin
runners_data.comment: Third over 1m here on sole 2yo start; pedigree suggests that he will relish this trip
runners_data.spotlight: Having been outpaced he kept on for a promising third at 8-1 on debut here (1m, good to firm) last August; gelded since; his pedigree suggests that he will relish this step up in trip on his reappearance; strong contender.

runners_data.name: N'Ion
runners_data.comment: There's potential in his pedigree but well beaten at big odds last month on first two runs
runners_data.spotlight: There's potential in his pedigree but he was well beaten at big odds last month on his first two starts (1m4f/9.4f, AW).

races.name: Ripon Silver Bowl Handicap

runners_data.name: Storm Esme
runners_data.note: Natural leader returning from 184-day break but class advantage evident from debut win, needs to handle longer absence
runners_data.comment: 2-3 as a 2yo, looking a nice prospect; her trainer has won this race four times since 2016
runners_data.spotlight: Well backed prior to her winning debut at Newcastle (6f) last September; failed to fire in the Redcar Two-Year-Old Trophy on second start but back on the up when defying a penalty in a Leicester novice in October (6f, good); the form of her two victories hasn't really worked out but she could do no more than win in decisive fashion and it is likely she has more to come; interesting for the stable that took this in 2016, 2019, 2022 and 2024.

runners_data.name: Bye Law
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with good 6f record on similar ground, Tim Easterby pair could work well together tactically
runners_data.comment: Two 6f wins in maiden/novice company; excuses for three nursery defeats; not discounted
runners_data.spotlight: Won 6f maiden/novice events last August (good/good to firm); unplaced in three nurseries afterwards but two of them were on soft ground and the other was a sound effort at York where 5f looked an inadequate test; gelded since last seen; returns on a reduced mark and one of two to consider for a stable with a fine record in the race.

runners_data.name: Hvar
runners_data.note: Changed yards over winter but similar RPR to previous form, prominent style suits the likely pace scenario
runners_data.comment: 6f AW win on final run for R Beckett; sold 26,000gns afterwards; opening mark demands more
runners_data.spotlight: Ran to a similar RPR in three runs for Ralph Beckett as a 2yo, getting off the mark in a small-field 6f novice at Wolverhampton when last seen in October; sold for 26,000gns soon afterwards; capable of better but such progress will be required to defy this mark.

runners_data.name: Mighty Magnus
runners_data.note: Front-running style but can press from just off the lead, gelding operation during break could sharpen him up
runners_data.comment: Made all in Ayr maiden last July (5.5f, good); fair nursery form afterwards; been gelded
runners_data.spotlight: Easy front-running win at Ayr (5.5f, good) last July on his third start; showed promise in nurseries afterwards; gelded during his six-month absence; personal best needed but it is not out of the question.

runners_data.name: Cotai Belle
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who may need faster pace than this race will provide, 5lb claimer Tindall takes pressure off
runners_data.comment: Two wins last summer before coming up short in good company; mark looks tough enough
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins last summer, a 5.5f maiden at Wetherby (good to firm) and a 5f nursery at Haydock (good), before coming up short in two sales races and the Listed Two-Year-Old Trophy; still has time on her side but not obviously well handicapped back from 194 days off.

runners_data.name: Rogue Temptation
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with 5lb claimer Rose Dawes, recent AW form suggests she's ready for turf return

runners_data.name: Wise Crack
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 212-day break, needs others to go fast early which seems unlikely here
runners_data.comment: Promising 7f AW run for former yard; sold 10,000gns in February; likely best watched
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in a 7f AW novice on his third run as a 2yo; well beaten over a mile when last seen in September; sold out of John Ryan's stable for 10,000gns in February; likely best watched on his stable/handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Wyle Cop
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good current form, 21 days since last run ideal and won't mind if pace gets strong
runners_data.comment: AW maiden win on return but couldn't build on it at Southwell last month; headgear on now
runners_data.spotlight: Promise as a 2yo and he only had to match that form to make a winning seasonal return at Wolverhampton last month; well backed back in handicap company at Southwell three weeks ago but he was ultimately a shade disappointing; connections now reach for headgear.

runners_data.name: Generous Rascal
runners_data.note: Showed ability on AW but step back to turf is question mark, prominent style suits race shape
runners_data.comment: 6f AW winner; outstayed over 7f on handicap debut; still has potential for new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Green on 2yo debut but took a big step forward when winning a 6f novice at Kempton on his second start (well backed); stiff task next time and his subsequent Southwell third (7f) was a solid start to his handicap career; sold out of Oliver Cole's stable for 35,000gns in February and gelded; new connections quick to drop him back to sprint trips and he remains with some potential

runners_data.name: Head For Freedom
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won over 5f, needs pace collapse or strong gallop to be effective over 6f
runners_data.comment: Ran okay in his first three nurseries but he needs to have improved over the winter
runners_data.spotlight: Won a 5f claimer at Beverley on his second start (last May) and he hit the frame in his first three nursery runs; failed to fire on the slowest ground he had tackled when last seen; needs to have improved over the winter if he is to make a winning return.

runners_data.name: Empress Olivia
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in career-best form, just 8 days since promising Catterick second gives fitness edge
runners_data.comment: C&D winner; good second on her reappearance last week; well drawn to attack
runners_data.spotlight: Always prominent when winning a C&D maiden last August; ran her best race in handicaps when second of ten in a 5f event at Catterick (good) last week, keeping on; she will have the stands' rail to help this time and should go well despite stepping up in class.

runners_data.name: Yy Spirit
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer switching yards, modest level of form and style may not suit moderate pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Won a 6f AW novice for Ed Bethell in December; sold 11,000gns since; mark looks tough
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at the fourth attempt when landing a modest fillies' novice (6f) at Newcastle four months ago; sold out of Ed Bethell's for 11,000gns in February; opening mark looks stiff.

runners_data.name: Fordham Flyer
runners_data.note: Prominent runner stepping up to 6f for first time, needs the extra distance to suit but style fits race
runners_data.comment: Promise over 5f last autumn; 6f should suit but improvement essential to defy opening mark
runners_data.spotlight: Two promising runs over 5f for this yard last autumn; stepping up to 6f should be in his favour and he is open to improvement but such progress looks essential if he is to defy this mark.

races.paceDynamic: Storm Esme is the sole confirmed front runner and will set a comfortable lead without pressure from the start. The prominent racers Bye Law, Hvar, Mighty Magnus, and Wyle Cop will sit just behind but none are natural pace-pressers over 6f. This creates a moderate tempo that builds gradually, with the real racing beginning in the final 2f as the hold-up horses Cotai Belle, Wise Crack, and Head For Freedom look to mount their challenges. This sustained pace scenario strongly favours the prominent racers who can track the leader without getting into an early speed duel, then kick clear when the hold-up horses are still finding their stride.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace stays moderate as expected with Storm Esme leading uncontested
scenarios.body: The prominent group can sit in perfect stalking positions and have the tactical advantage when the pace lifts, getting first run on the leaders while the closers are still too far back. Bye Law and Mighty Magnus are ideally positioned to capitalize on this race shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire Job
scenarios.trigger: If Storm Esme gets an easy lead and the prominent horses fail to apply enough pressure
scenarios.body: Her class advantage becomes decisive as she can dictate terms throughout and has enough left for the finish, with the field leaving their runs too late. The 184-day break could actually help her freshness in a tactical race like this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge Success
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes stronger than expected in the middle stages as prominent horses jostle for position
scenarios.body: The closers get the perfect setup as the early leaders and stalkers weaken, allowing horses like Wise Crack and Head For Freedom to sweep past tired legs. This requires the front group to go too hard too early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Storm Esme goes too slowly early and creates a sprint finish from the 2f pole
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure speed test over 2f where any horse can win regardless of early position, favoring those with natural pace like Empress Olivia who showed good speed when winning recently. Form and class become less relevant in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Storm Esme's market support will reveal connections' confidence after the long break - strong money suggests she's ready to fire fresh
Watch the early fractions as Mighty Magnus or Wyle Cop could press Storm Esme harder than expected and change the race dynamic completely
Empress Olivia's quick return from Catterick suggests she's thriving - any positive body language in the preliminaries makes her dangerous
If Bye Law and Hvar both track Storm Esme closely, the Easterby pair could dominate with tactical advantage over single-yard runners
Market moves on the hold-up horses like Wise Crack or Cotai Belle would suggest connections expect a stronger pace than appears likely

races.name: Armstrong Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Sixtygeesbaby
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for in-form David O'Meara stable, good recent Newmarket second suggests retained ability despite poor stable debut
runners_data.comment: Unexposed 4yo; not well drawn on stable/seasonal debut; remains of serious interest
runners_data.spotlight: Ended 2025 with a good second at Newmarket (6f, good), after which he changed hands for 50,000gns; only eighth (of 19) on his stable debut at Doncaster 18 days ago but he wasn't well drawn as things panned out and he ran as though the run would bring him on; remains a sprinter of interest.

runners_data.name: Kats Bob
runners_data.note: Front-running enthusiast fully effective over course and distance, made encouraging seasonal return with apprentice claim valuable
runners_data.comment: Front-runner; shone in 2025 and last week's return to action was a good one; contender
runners_data.spotlight: Enthusiastic front-runner who shone for Ruth Carr in 2025, winning five 6f handicaps; fully effective over C&D and he made an encouraging seasonal return at Catterick last week, second of nine having been headed inside the final furlong (6f, good); looks the likeliest leader up the far side if the field split.

runners_data.name: It Just Takes Time
runners_data.note: Prominent racer but unconvincing Doncaster return and better over 7f+ suggests others preferred at this trip
runners_data.comment: Low-key return to action last month and may be better suited by 7f+ nowadays
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner in 2023 off an 8lb higher mark; all his subsequent wins have come over 7f+ and his return to action at Doncaster was unconvincing; others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Kodiac Thriller
runners_data.note: Prominent type who did well for this yard last season, stands' rail group form suggests ability to handle big fields
runners_data.comment: Did well last year, including over C&D; on a handy mark but his reappearance was low key
runners_data.spotlight: Prominent-racer; did well for this yard last year, winning at Thirsk in May and running several good races in defeat, notably when best of the stands' rail group in the Great St Wilfrid over C&D; he needs to leave his low-key seasonal return well behind if he is to feature today though.

runners_data.name: Fortamour
runners_data.note: Course specialist with two previous wins in this race, veteran's consistency over track gives him strong each-way claims
runners_data.comment: Record in this race reads 1413; drying ground not ideal but can't rule out at this venue
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran who has been a regular in this event, winning in 2022 (soft) and 2024 (heavy) and hitting the frame in both 2023 and 2025; ended 2025 campaign with a pair of AW wins but he hasn't been at that level in either run this year; drying ground not ideal but he can never be ruled out completely at this track.

runners_data.name: Almarada Prince
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse stepping back up in trip, recent all-weather form encouraging for Paul Midgley stable
runners_data.comment: On a dangerous mark and both runs for new yard have been encouraging enough; not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to win in 2025 but he has edged down the weights and his two AW runs for Paul Midgley have both been encouraging enough; no issue with the return to turf; type to win races sooner rather than later.

runners_data.name: American Style
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 207-day break, won on seasonal debut at this meeting last year for Kevin Ryan
runners_data.comment: C&D win on this card last year; ended 2025 tamely; likely to be seen to better effect here
runners_data.spotlight: Prominent racer; C&D winner on his seasonal return on this card 12 months ago; often ran well in good handicaps afterwards and although he ended 2025 with a couple of lesser efforts, he is likely to be seen to much better effect this time; should make a bold bid up the stands' rail.

runners_data.name: Mister Sox
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with excellent course record including hat-trick completion here, returning from long absence for Tim Easterby
runners_data.comment: Good C&D form in a productive 2025 campaign; has gone well fresh; one to take seriously
runners_data.spotlight: Made a flying start to his 2025 campaign, his win in a C&D handicap last May completing a hat-trick; added another C&D handicap in August and also ran a fine race in a Class 2 here in September (off this mark); that C&D form makes him an interesting candidate for a stable with two wins in the race since 2019.

runners_data.name: Rock Opera
runners_data.note: Hold-up sprinter on losing streak but well handicapped, long absence and big field concerns for connections
runners_data.comment: Losing run of 20 has seen him drop down the weights; yet to run well in four visits here
runners_data.spotlight: Hold-up sprinter and on a losing run of 20; well handicapped as a consequence and should be winning soon; whether it will be today, after 166 days off and at a track where he is yet to run well, is debatable.

runners_data.name: Roberto Caro
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid recent all-weather form, keeping on strongly suggests fitness maintained
runners_data.comment: On last winning mark and he has run two solid races on AW this year; each-way shout
runners_data.spotlight: Won a Racing League handicap off this mark last summer; two solid AW efforts this year, keeping on strongly for third in a well-contested 6f handicap at Newcastle three weeks ago; each-way shout.

runners_data.name: Modern Times
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 302-day layoff, maiden winner here last season but big step up in class
runners_data.comment: 15th time lucky when winning a C&D maiden last June; absent since; returns in a warm race
runners_data.spotlight: Belatedly off the mark in a C&D maiden last June, his second run for Tim Easterby; more to do back in a competitive handicap after 302 days on the sidelines.

runners_data.name: Intervention
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with prolific all-weather record, Great St Wilfrid winner over course and distance last season
runners_data.comment: Made all in big C&D handicap last year off 3lb higher; good efffort latest; can't dismiss
runners_data.spotlight: Prolific winner down the year and although most of that success has come on AW, he did pick up a big pot on turf when making all in the Great St Wilfrid over C&D last August; ran well from a wide draw at Lingfield on Good Friday; on a dangerous mark but a central draw probably not ideal today.

runners_data.name: Wild Clary
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner with tactical advantage, consistent efforts including strong Haydock second suggest competitive chance
runners_data.comment: Infrequent winner but on handy mark and should be sharper with a recent run behind him
runners_data.spotlight: Just one win to his name after 13 starts but he ended his 3yo campaign with two fine efforts, notably when chasing home a well-backed sprinter at Haydock in September (6f, good to soft; traffic problems at a crucial stage), and his return to action at Kempton should have blown away any cobwebs; best efforts on flat tracks but he is feasibly weighted if the undulations of Ripon aren't an issue.

runners_data.name: Wen Moon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 162-day break, better over 5f than 6f based on recent form pattern

runners_data.name: Another Investment
runners_data.note: Hold-up type known for fading in finish, needs to overcome poor reappearance effort despite lower mark
runners_data.comment: On a dangerous mark but there were more bad days than good in 2025; yet to shine here
runners_data.spotlight: More modest runs than good ones in 2025 but he did bolt up at Doncaster last June (6f, good to firm) and he is 4lb lower now; needs to leave his reappearance effort well behind him and he has finished down the field in his two visits here.

runners_data.name: Lesley's Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 145-day absence, course and distance nursery winner but struggled with handicapper subsequently
runners_data.comment: C&D winner; struggled for much of 2025; returns to action in a deep race
runners_data.spotlight: Won two of his first three starts, including a C&D nursery off 8lb higher, but the handicapper was in command for much of 2025; creditable third to Fortamour at Newcastle when last seen 145 days ago but he has more on his plate in this deeper race.

races.paceDynamic: Wild Clary is the only confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner field, with multiple prominent racers including Kats Bob, Sixtygeesbaby, It Just Takes Time, and Kodiac Thriller likely to press early. The large field and singular pace angle suggests Wild Clary can dictate comfortable fractions without serious early pressure. With so many hold-up horses including Mister Sox, Rock Opera, Intervention, and Wen Moon needing to navigate traffic in the closing stages, this race shape strongly favours the early-positioned horses who can secure clean runs and avoid the scramble.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Clary gets an easy lead with the prominent racers settling just behind rather than pressuring
scenarios.body: Wild Clary controls the tempo and has enough left to resist late challenges, while the hold-up horses get caught in traffic with too much to do. The early pace advantage proves decisive in a large field where clean runs are at a premium.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent racers apply some pressure to Wild Clary but still travel well into the straight
scenarios.body: The early-positioned horses have first run on the field while the hold-up brigade struggle for racing room. One of the prominent racers times their challenge perfectly to collar the leader late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses and becomes stop-start with prominent racers getting in each other's way
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the 2f marker, allowing the strongest finishers to weave through and deliver telling late runs. Hold-up horses with the best turn of foot capitalize on the messy early positioning.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If both the leader and prominent racers go too fast early in response to the large field pressure
scenarios.body: The early leaders come back to the field dramatically in the final furlong, allowing a well-positioned hold-up horse on a low weight to surge through. A forgotten runner gets the perfect trip behind the pace collapse.

watchPoints.text: Wild Clary's early position is crucial - if he gets uncontested lead the race could be over before it starts
Watch for traffic problems affecting Mister Sox, Rock Opera and other hold-up horses in such a large field
Monitor if Kats Bob or other prominent racers put pressure on Wild Clary early which could set up back-runners
American Style's fitness after 207 days off will be evident in the first two furlongs
The draw and early positioning will be critical with 16 runners over this straight 6f course

races.name: Ripon "Cock O' The North" Handicap

runners_data.name: Austrian Theory
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 178 days with poor recent form but previous course form on good ground
runners_data.comment: 0-10 last year but placed a few times, including on last two starts last autumn
runners_data.spotlight: 0-10 last year but runner-up on his reappearance last April (1m, good) and placed off today's mark on his final two outings last autumn (1m2f, good to soft/soft); might not be far away on this return to action.

runners_data.name: Raulin
runners_data.note: Front-running tendencies but 203-day layoff raises fitness concerns despite previous 1m2f success
runners_data.comment: Three wins last year and he might be the type to continue to progress this season
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who won on handicap debut at Redcar (1m2f, good to soft) last May and scored twice in a row at Pontefract (1m2f good/good to firm) last summer; unplaced on final run last year and has to prove his current mark is within range, but he might be the type to continue to progress this season.

runners_data.name: Sir William
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but disappointing recent AW debut suggests needs this run after winter break
runners_data.comment: Underwhelming on stable debut but may have needed the run; progressive last season
runners_data.spotlight: Underwhelming fifth of six on last month's stable and seasonal debut at Southwell (1m3f, AW), but he was wide early and may have needed the run; progressive on turf last season for William Haggas and he could tap back into that promise and play a leading role today.

runners_data.name: Financer
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse on 187-day break, twice placed in this race previously but headgear addition suggests issues
runners_data.comment: 0-11 last year but runner-up three times, including in this race on his reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: 0-11 last year when not at his best on his final few runs; however, he was runner-up three times last season, including in this race on his reappearance (good), and he's 2lb lower 12 months on; capable of having a big say.

runners_data.name: Spioradalta
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with excellent recent Doncaster run and two previous course wins, key contender
runners_data.comment: Five wins last year (two C&D); respectable reappearance; could show benefit of that run
runners_data.spotlight: Five wins last year (various ground), two of them over C&D, and campaign concluded with good third at Redcar in November; respectable reappearance run at Doncaster recently and could show the benefit of that outing today.

runners_data.name: Cristo
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with poor AW form but headgear addition and Richard Hannon stable in decent form

runners_data.name: Glistening Nights
runners_data.note: Prominent style on attractive mark but 200-day layoff against him despite past course success
runners_data.comment: On a handy mark on last August's form & could be a contender for last year's winning yard
runners_data.spotlight: Down the field on final two runs last season but he may have been ready for a break; on a handy mark based on his form last August and could be a contender for last year's winning yard.

runners_data.name: Lunar Eclipse
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare whose recent AW form reads poorly and faces difficult task from back
runners_data.comment: Twice well beaten last November but has had a break since; of interest on earlier form
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in Listed race and AW handicap on final two runs in November; however, a break may have helped and she's of interest judged on her two efforts last summer (1m1f/8.3f), when shaping as though 1m2f would suit.

runners_data.name: Spoken Truth
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with promising Doncaster fourth on stable debut, lightly raced with potential upside
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced 5yo who was a promising fourth on recent stable debut; on the shortlist
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to progress for Dermot Weld but this lightly raced 5yo was a promising fourth at Doncaster (1m2f, good to soft) on his recent stable and seasonal debut; could have more to offer for this yard; on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Pomme Pomme
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with 5lb apprentice claim returning after 237 days but with strong course record
runners_data.comment: Prolific last year after moving into handicaps; no surprise to see a bold bid on return
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who won her first five handicaps (8.6f/1m2f) last May/June and campaign concluded with close second of three to a progressive filly at Hamilton (1m1f) in August; no surprise to see a bold bid on her return, provided conditions suit (unproven on slow ground).

races.paceDynamic: Pomme Pomme will lead from the flag as the only confirmed front-runner, likely joined by prominent runners Spioradalta and Glistening Nights in the early positions. With most of the field comprising hold-up horses (Austrian Theory, Raulin, Sir William, Financer, Cristo, Lunar Eclipse, Spoken Truth), the pace should be genuine but sustainable through the middle sections. The large contingent of hold-up horses will create a cavalry charge from the back straight, but the lack of early pace pressure means Pomme Pomme can dictate terms and the prominent runners can travel into contention. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will plague the hold-up brigade in a small field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Pomme Pomme gets an uncontested lead and maintains stamina over 1m2f
scenarios.body: She can kick clear turning for home while the hold-up horses get caught in traffic behind a slowly-run race. Rose Dawes' 5lb claim becomes crucial in a tight finish against late challengers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Spioradalta or Glistening Nights can track Pomme Pomme and outstay her
scenarios.body: The prominent runners get first run on the field while maintaining better tactical positions than the hold-up horses. Jason Hart's shrewd positioning on Spioradalta proves decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly sedate and the field bunches up turning in
scenarios.body: The superior class horses get clear runs and their finishing kicks prove decisive despite poor positioning. Spoken Truth's recent Doncaster fourth suggests returning form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the favorites falter after long layoffs and race fitness tells
scenarios.body: A horse with recent form like Cristo or Sir William capitalizes on others' ring-rustiness. Kevin Ryan's 1/19 record suggests Lunar Eclipse faces an uphill task.

watchPoints.text: Pomme Pomme sets too strong an early pace given her 237-day layoff and fades badly in the straight
Traffic problems develop in the straight as multiple hold-up horses seek room simultaneously in a small field
Rose Dawes handles the tactical demands of front-running in her first ride back from a winter break
Spioradalta's recent Doncaster run was better than it appeared and Jason Hart has him perfectly positioned
Austrian Theory shows early signs of a revival after a disappointing 2023 campaign for Tim Easterby

races.name: Racing BetBuilder At Spreadex Sports Handicap

runners_data.name: Saxon Prince
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front runner gives him tactical edge despite moderate recent form and 45-day layoff
runners_data.comment: The step up in trip is worth a go on stable debut and he's one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: All five runs for Clive Cox on AW, going close in four-runner handicap at Kempton (7f) last month; sold for 24,000gns since; has shaped as though this step up to 1m is worth a go; one to consider on stable/turf debut.

runners_data.name: Gwen's Girl
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits race shape but 181-day break and trainer's poor strike rate are concerns
runners_data.comment: Second on debut last September; two lesser runs followed but not ruled out on h'cap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Kept on for second on debut at Carlisle (6f, soft) last September; two lesser runs followed (6f/1m, AW/good) but she retains potential in view of that initial promise, and she's not ruled out on handicap/seasonal debut.

runners_data.name: Domination
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with tactical advantage but showed little in three juvenile starts and long absence
runners_data.comment: Failed to threaten across his four 2yo starts; has to raise his game on stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Well-bred sort but he failed to threaten on his three 2yo starts for Clive Cox, the latest his handicap debut at Nottingham (1m, good) in October; sold for 16,000gns later that month; has to raise his game on stable debut.

runners_data.name: Sailor Batt
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces traffic issues despite consistent placed efforts and recent Newcastle third
runners_data.comment: Remains a maiden after nine starts but placed a few times, including last month (1m, AW)
runners_data.spotlight: Remains a maiden after nine starts but he's been runner-up in two handicaps (including on turf) and was a close third at Newcastle (1m, AW) most recently; every chance he'll be thereabouts once more.

runners_data.name: Singarda
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 211-day break but has had wind surgery which could unlock improvement
runners_data.comment: Just one good run among his four 2yo starts but attractive mark on that York effort
runners_data.spotlight: Down the field on three of his four 2yo starts, most recently on handicap debut at Beverley (8.4f, soft) in September when last seen; however, he's had wind surgery since and is on an attractive mark judged on his sixth of 16 at York (7f, good) last July; could be a contender.

runners_data.name: Walk On Walk On
runners_data.note: Hold-up style problematic in this field composition despite showing ability in Ireland previously
runners_data.comment: Showed ability last year but improvement is needed if he's to make a winning stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Displayed ability among his six (winless) 2yo starts for Des Donovan; sold for 7,750gns last October and gelded since; however, improvement is needed in first-time cheekpieces if he's to make a winning stable debut.

runners_data.name: Norcross Brow
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs luck in running but has solid placed form including turf runner-up effort
runners_data.comment: 0-6 but has shown promise and the first-time hood could help him settle better; chance
runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 but has twice finished runner-up (including on turf) and he was denied a clear run when sixth of nine, beaten only about 2l, at Newcastle (1m, AW) last time; the first-time hood could help him settle better; chance.

runners_data.name: Fickle McSelfish
runners_data.note: Turf debut for AW winner but cheekpieces retained and recent winning form provides confidence
runners_data.comment: Won in good style at Newcastle then raced wide early when third at Southwell
runners_data.spotlight: All seven starts on AW; got off the mark at the sixth attempt in first-time cheekpieces (retained) at Newcastle (7f) last month, doing it comfortably from the front; third under a penalty at Southwell (7f) seven days later and now another 4lb higher, but he raced wide early last time and may yet to have more to offer in the headgear; chance if seeing out 1m.

runners_data.name: Leysthorpe Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up style and fading tendency clash but rock-bottom weight and half-brother to winners
runners_data.comment: Half-brother to four winners who goes handicapping off a basement mark for in-form yard
runners_data.spotlight: He didn't show much in the winter on his first three starts (7f/1m, AW); however, this half-brother to four winners goes handicapping off a basement mark for his in-form yard and is a possible improver; interesting, all the more so if attracting market support.

runners_data.name: Ciao Capo
runners_data.note: AW winner needs to transfer form to turf but gelding operation may have freshened him up
runners_data.comment: Comfortable win on AW when last seen; player if continuing the good work back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: He got better with each of his three runs in nurseries last autumn, winning comfortably at Newcastle (1m, AW) in November; gelded since; he needs to transfer his improvement back to turf but is bred to do better still and a 6lb rise might not stop him if he can continue the good work.

runners_data.name: Hood Wink
runners_data.note: Blinkers back on after neck defeat when last wearing them, gelded since and low weight helps
runners_data.comment: 0-7 last year but went close the only time he wore these blinkers; gelded since last start
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7 last year but the only time he wore these blinkers he was beaten just a neck at Redcar (1m, good to soft) in September; gelded since his last run in November; no surprise if he has a part to play on reappearance.

races.paceDynamic: Saxon Prince will take this field along as the only confirmed front runner, with Gwen's Girl, Domination, and possibly Sailor Batt tracking in behind. The pace should be sustainable rather than frantic given the lack of genuine speed horses, allowing the large contingent of hold-up horses to get competitive. With 8 of 11 runners employing hold-up tactics on a flat Ripon mile, this race will become a sprint finish from the 2f marker. This tactical setup strongly favours prominent racers who can position handy and kick, rather than the mass of hold-up horses who will face a traffic nightmare.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Saxon Prince sets a steady pace and the prominent horses get first run
scenarios.body: The handful of prominent racers avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will engulf the large pack of hold-up horses in the straight. Saxon Prince and Gwen's Girl can use their tactical advantage to dictate terms.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses gets a dream run through traffic
scenarios.body: A single hold-up horse finds racing room while others are trapped, capitalizing on their superior finishing kick. The winner will be the one jockey who navigates the crowded finish best.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Benefits Outsiders
scenarios.trigger: If the finish becomes completely congested with interference
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery where the least fancied horses with the clearest runs prevail over better-rated but hampered rivals. Hood Wink and Leysthorpe Star's low weights become crucial advantages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Saxon Prince Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Saxon Prince kicks clear turning for home with no serious challengers
scenarios.body: The front runner exploits the tactical disadvantage of the massed hold-up horses who leave their runs too late on the stiff Ripon finish. None of the closers can reel him in despite his moderate recent form.

watchPoints.text: Saxon Prince could steal this if the hold-up brigade leave their runs too late in the straight
Traffic problems will be severe with 8 hold-up horses - watch for interference and hard luck stories
Gwen's Girl's 181-day absence is lengthy but her debut second suggests ability if returning fit
Fickle McSelfish making turf debut but cheekpieces help and trainer has recent winner with stable in form
Hood Wink returns to blinkers which produced his best effort when beaten a neck last September

races.name: Go Racing In Yorkshire Apprentice Handicap (Yorkshire Future Stars Apprentice Series)

runners_data.name: Garden Oasis
runners_data.note: Lead runner getting uncontested fractions but 190 days off and age 11 creates stamina doubts late
runners_data.comment: 11yo; below par at the end of last season but ran well in this on his comeback last April
runners_data.spotlight: 11yo who was below par at the end of last season but reappeared last April with a good fourth in this race (good) and picked up three wins subsequently; he's 3lb below his last winning mark and is not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Empirestateofmind
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but poor reappearance form and seller win last time suggests decline
runners_data.comment: Two wins last year and may have needed reappearance outing in the Spring Mile
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins last year (1m/1m1f, good/soft); the last of them came in a seller and he was well beaten on last month's reappearance at Doncaster, but that was the competitive Spring Mile and he may have needed the run; won this in 2022 and he's not discounted off a handy mark.

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suits this race shape despite long losing run
runners_data.comment: Runner-up five times last May-August but went off the boil in the autumn; reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up five times last May-August and he's on an attractive mark on that form; however, he went off the boil in the autumn and his long losing run continues; needs to get back on track on this reappearance.

runners_data.name: Walsingham
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong 2023 form but 173 days layoff creates fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: 3-3 last year prior to October heavy-ground defeat; could still have more left in the tank
runners_data.spotlight: Made it 3-3 for the year (1m, good/soft) when winning at Ascot last September; well beaten at Doncaster in October but on heavy ground; this is his first run since and he could still have more left in the tank.

runners_data.name: Cosmos Raj
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner back to last winning mark after 195-day break
runners_data.comment: Three wins last May/July & is on last winning mark; may improve for this reappearance run
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins last May/July at about 1m on various ground and he's back down to his last winning mark; may have been ready for a break towards end of last season but there's a suspicion he'll improve for this comeback run.

runners_data.name: Mr Mistoffelees
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but poor turf record compared to AW success
runners_data.comment: Won at Newcastle last October but in blinkers, not the cheekpieces he wears today
runners_data.spotlight: In good form in blinkers towards the end of last year, winning at Newcastle (1m, AW) in October; however, he has a poor strike-rate and wasn't at his best in cheekpieces at Newcastle (1m, AW) three weeks ago following a break; cheekpieces remain on today.

runners_data.name: On The River
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who prefers soft ground but was second in this race last year
runners_data.comment: Second in this last year and reappeared with promising fifth at Doncaster; in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: The vast majority of his wins have come on slow ground but the going was good when he was second in this race last year; reappeared with promising fifth of 22 in the Spring Mile at Doncaster and could be in the mix.

runners_data.name: Good Morning Alex
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with course and distance dead-heat but poor recent AW form
runners_data.comment: Well handicapped on turf form last April/June but hasn't shone on AW this year
runners_data.spotlight: Dead-heated over C&D (good) last April and went very close at Carlisle in June; well handicapped on that form but a long way below his best on AW this year; the return to turf needs to trigger a major revival.

runners_data.name: Chesneys Charm
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner stepping up to mile for first time since winning at 7f
runners_data.comment: Needs to build on last month's comeback at Southwell and the blinkers are left off
runners_data.spotlight: Won off this mark in first-time blinkers at York (7f, good) last July and he could improve for last month's respectable comeback at Southwell (7f, AW); however, he does need to build on that and blinkers are left off.

runners_data.name: Milteye
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who was tailed off last time but may have needed the run
runners_data.comment: Won three times last year and could leave his reappearance performance miles behind
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off on last month's reappearance in the Spring Mile at Doncaster but may have needed the run and those ridden more patiently came to the fore; he won three times last year (1m1f/1m, soft/good) and it will be no surprise if he leaves that latest performance miles behind.

races.paceDynamic: Garden Oasis will be the sole confirmed pace-setter but won't face early pressure, allowing him to dictate a steady tempo. The real danger comes at the 3-2 furlong pole where Empirestateofmind, Walsingham, Good Morning Alex and Milteye all want prominent positions, creating inevitable traffic problems. This compressed field setup means the hold-up horses like Barley, Mr Mistoffelees, On The River, Cosmos Raj and Chesneys Charm can cruise into contention without pace pressure. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up runners who can avoid the mid-race squeeze and time their challenge perfectly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Garden Oasis sets steady fractions and the prominent group creates traffic problems turning in
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows patient riders to position perfectly while the prominent congestion creates winning opportunities for those held up. Barley and Cosmos Raj benefit most from this tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Garden Oasis wires field
scenarios.trigger: If Garden Oasis gets uncontested early fractions and the prominent runners fail to challenge decisively
scenarios.body: The 11-year-old can dictate throughout and kick clear when the traffic-hampered pack tries to organize late. His three wins last season prove he can capitalize when getting his own way up front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent runners prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Walsingham or Empirestateofmind can secure the ideal stalking position without getting boxed
scenarios.body: One of the prominent runners avoids the traffic and gets first run on Garden Oasis turning for home. Walsingham's three wins last season make him most likely to execute this tactical plan.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Speed holds throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Garden Oasis sets stronger fractions than expected and the closers get caught too far back
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure becomes irrelevant as the leaders maintain their advantage to the line. Good Morning Alex's course and distance dead-heat gives him the best credentials from this position.

Monitor Garden Oasis for stamina concerns in final furlong after 190-day layoff at age 11
Check if Barley and Cosmos Raj can overcome long losing runs despite suitable race shape
Watch Walsingham for fitness after 173-day break despite strong 2023 winning form
Observe if the hold-up horses can organize their challenges without getting caught too far back
